I'm hiring a Social Media & Content Manager to join my team 🎯

I'm looking for someone to take real ownership of my content and social strategy. Someone who is not just executing posts, but understanding my audience deeply and running the engine that turns content into growth. This is a hands-on role for someone who wants to build something with me, not just manage a calendar.

What you'll own

Weekly reporting on total posts, total IG views, email/Manychat leads collected, and trials to my fitness app offering driven from social. You'll be close enough to the numbers to know what's actually moving the needle and help iterate from there.

Phase 1 — Get to know my audience

You'll dig into my DMs, community messages, in-app chat, and survey responses to build a real picture of who my audience is: their desired outcome, their biggest issues, and their limiting beliefs. From there, you'll define my content pillars and build out a swipe file of viral, high-performing content across those pillars to draw inspiration from (likely living in Notion).
Phase 2 — Run the content engine

Using a 70/20/10 approach, you'll manage my content pipeline: 70% doubling down on what's already working, 20% smart variations you develop, and 10% brand-new ideas you pitch and test (2–4 fresh concepts a week). You'll own my trial reels engine — 1–3 highly viral reels a day within my content pillars — handling post creation end to end, and reporting weekly on what worked, what didn't, and why.
Phase 3 — Grow beyond Instagram

Once Instagram is running like a well-oiled machine, we'll look at expanding to Facebook, YouTube Shorts, TikTok, and Pinterest, and figure out what team/support that would need.

What you need

Experience working in the social media creator space is a must — you should understand creator content, platform trends, and what makes short-form video perform. Experience in fitness is a plus! Beyond that, you should be comfortable going deep on research and audience psychology, then turning that into content that performs. I'm looking for someone who thrives on researching, testing, and iterating and has a passion for content creation!

About the Role We're hiring a Production Manager
to own the day-to-day execution of website projects and recurring SEO deliverables. You'll establish internal schedules, assign and prioritize work, manage team capacity, lead daily production check-ins, oversee quality standards, and ensure commitments are met.

This is an internal production leadership role, not a hands-on designer, developer, or SEO specialist position
. You'll need strong website production knowledge and the confidence to direct specialists, address missed deadlines, and resolve bottlenecks.

You'll have authority over internal assignments, deadlines, and priorities, but no direct reports. You'll document recurring performance concerns and escalate formal personnel matters to leadership. Account Managers own all client communication; you own internal production execution.

Your job is to ensure the right work gets completed correctly and on time, without constant leadership intervention.

Key ResponsibilitiesWebsite Production Create and own internal schedules, assignments, priorities, and deadlines for active website projects.
Understand website discovery, copywriting, design, development, QA, and launch dependencies to sequence work appropriately.
Assign work across designers, developers, writers, and other specialists based on capacity and deadlines.
Monitor progress daily; identify stalled tasks, bottlenecks, and delivery risks before deadlines are missed.
Coordinate internal handoffs and communicate timeline changes to Account Managers and leadership.
Keep website production plans, ownership, and task statuses accurate in Monday.com.

SEO Production Own production operations for recurring monthly SEO deliverables, including scheduling, prioritization, workflow, and delivery consistency.
Work with SEO specialists to turn their strategies and planned deliverables into clear assignments and deadlines.
Coordinate content, optimization, technical SEO, and related tasks across specialists, writers, and developers.
Track completed, outstanding, and at-risk work for each SEO client; address delays before monthly commitments are missed.
Ensure established QA procedures are followed and recurring delivery problems are identified.

SEO specialists own strategy and technical execution. The Production Manager owns operational follow-through and timely delivery.

Daily Leadership & Accountability Lead daily production check-ins to clarify priorities, progress, blockers, and next steps.
Set clear expectations for task ownership, deadlines, and completion standards.
Follow up consistently, address missed commitments directly, and prevent overdue work from accumulating.
Rebalance assignments with specialists when workloads are unrealistic; communicate resulting timeline impacts.
Independently reprioritize production work to meet business commitments.
Document repeated missed deadlines or performance concerns and report them to leadership.

Quality & Workflow Oversight Ensure specialists complete technical QA and work meets established requirements before being marked complete.
Spot-check deliverables for completeness, accuracy, and adherence to production standards.
Return substandard work to the responsible specialist with clear corrections and a revised deadline.
Track recurring quality problems and recommend improvements to reduce rework.
Identify inefficient handoffs, scheduling problems, and production bottlenecks; recommend practical process improvements.

Monday.com, Reporting & Collaboration Use Monday.com
to actively manage assignments, deadlines, dependencies, workload, and project status.
Maintain live visibility into overdue work, upcoming milestones, and production capacity.
Prepare weekly production scorecards and risk updates for the Vice President / Integrator.
Coordinate regularly with Account Managers so they can accurately manage client expectations.
Communicate production risks proactively and escalate issues requiring leadership decisions.
Maintain clear internal documentation and reinforce accurate task updates across the team.

Division of Responsibility Production Manager:
Internal schedules, assignments, priorities, workload balancing, production accountability, SEO delivery tracking, quality oversight, and reporting.
Account Managers:
Client relationships, communication, expectations, information collection, feedback, and approvals.
Production Specialists:
Technical execution, specialist-level QA, technical recommendations, and SEO strategy where applicable.

QualificationsRequired Demonstrated experience managing production workflows, digital projects, or delivery operations; proven ownership matters more than a specific number of years
.
Strong understanding of website development phases, dependencies, QA, and launch processes.
Direct Monday.com experience
managing projects, tasks, and deadlines.
Proven ability to establish schedules, assign work, prioritize competing demands, and enforce deadlines.
Experience coordinating multiple concurrent projects or recurring deliverables.
Strong organizational skills, attention to detail, follow-through, and independent judgment.
Confidence leading production meetings, addressing missed commitments, and holding contributors accountable.
Ability to identify capacity constraints, production risks, and quality concerns early.
Clear written and verbal communication and effective collaboration with technical and client-facing teams.
Ability to work in Charlotte, NC, under CGN's hybrid schedule.

Preferred Experience in a digital marketing, creative, or website development agency.
Familiarity with SEO workflows, content production, and recurring monthly deliverables.
Experience coordinating designers, developers, copywriters, and SEO specialists.
Experience building production dashboards, scorecards, or process improvements.
Familiarity with CMS platforms, website QA, UX, and SEO fundamentals.

What Success Looks Like On-Time Delivery:
Website production milestones and monthly SEO deliverables are completed on schedule. Overdue work is actively resolved and risks are flagged early.
Quality:
Deliverables meet requirements, specialist QA is completed, and corrections are tracked through resolution.
Workload Management:
Team members have clear assignments and deadlines; priorities and capacity are adjusted proactively.
Production Visibility:
Monday.com reflects accurate progress, and weekly reporting gives leadership reliable insight into delivery performance.
Specific targets will be established using CGN's production standards and commitments.

The Right Person for This Role You take ownership without waiting for direction. You're organized, decisive, and comfortable setting expectations and having direct conversations when commitments are missed. You understand how creative and technical work moves through production, spot risks early, and use accurate data to make decisions. You care about quality, communicate proactively, and follow through until work is complete.
This role isn't a fit for someone who only monitors task lists, avoids accountability conversations, or waits until deadlines have passed to intervene.

Company match of up to 4%.

Professional Development:
Industry certifications, training, and ongoing learning opportunities.
Clients:
Work with quality-driven, high-end interior remodeling contractors who value long-term partnerships.

Location:
Charlotte, NC.

First 90 days fully in-office; afterward, three days in-office and two remote days weekly.
